additional_considerations.rationale: Degenerative spine disease can compress nerves like herniation or fracture, but its time course is usually more chronic than in this case.
Age-related changes that would cause a slowly progressive radiculopathy.
A possible spinal lesion with weight loss in an older woman raises concern for bone metastasis, most likely from breast.
A rarer cause of spinal lesions; may come with anemia, renal failure, hypercalcemia and constitutional symptoms.

source_issues: The script asks 'Any known allergies?' (topic Drug Allergies) with no patient answer, so the parsed qa has no allergy item; the note gives 'No known drug allergies' (added as from_note fact f039).
Exam e005: 'Babinski reflex is 8 bilaterally' is an OCR artifact (probably a downgoing/negative symbol); direction not stated, recorded neutrally (x014).

Exam e005 records Kernig and Brudzinski signs as positive, which fits neither the history (no fever, headache, photophobia) nor the gold; possibly an error for 'negative'. Recorded as written (x017). The checklist spells it 'Kemig'.

Note HPI says 'left upper extremity numbness'; the script answer to the weakness/numbness question reports only tingling of the left arm, while sp_notes ask the SP to pretend numbness in the back of the left forearm.
The weight-loss/fever/night-sweats answer (p014) does not explicitly deny fever or night sweats; the denials come from the note HPI. The note's 'No dyspnea' was not asked in the script.
p016 'Do you experience any health problems?' is answered 'No', yet p018 reveals osteopenia found at screening (note PMH: 'Osteopenia on last DEXA').
Script says the mother 'had' osteoporosis; the note says she 'has' it. Parents' living status is not given although asked.
Gold #1 exam finding 'spasm' is not documented in the note exam.
The challenging question starts with a doubled quotation mark ('""I am scheduled...'); cleaned in persona.
annotator_notes: p002 'Since then it hurts to move' and p009 'Turning my head in either direction' are merged into one aggravating-factor fact (f003) to avoid a paraphrase duplicate.
f012 (left arm numbness) is note-only and flagged; the SP's simulated forearm numbness is also recorded as exam finding x018.
f026 records the literal 'No' to health problems; osteopenia is kept as a separate present PMH fact (f030).
Family history marked historical because the patient uses the past tense and the parents' living status is not stated.
The patient-description line 'lives with her husband' exists only in raw_opening; kept in persona.acting_notes because source ids cannot point to it.
The upcoming trip to visit her sister in Florida in three days appears only in the challenging question (persona.patient_questions).
